amendments.change: Three new strategies added: rollback_with_reflection (source: arXiv 2609.18304 — same rollback as source_rollback plus verbal note in restored trajectory), verbal_correction (source: arXiv 2605.06737 / Reflexion / CRITIC — one-step rollback with corrected result pre-fetched), adaptive (source: arXiv 2608.11977 — fault-type-aware meta-strategy routing to empirically best method). Phase 4b runs these three strategies on task 0, seeds 300-302, all 3 faults using gemini-3.5-flash-lite for direct comparison with Phases 1-3. controlled_runs_planned updated from 162 to 216 (3 tasks x 3 seeds-base x 3 faults x 9 strategies + 3 new-strategy rows for seeds 300-302). unfaulted references unchanged at 9 for task-0 base seeds.

scope: Controlled recovery extension using official released retail tasks, tools, policy and unchanged evaluator; distinct from unmodified benchmark results
injection_rule: First successful get_user_details response, one injection per run; never reinject after rollback
source_detector: Earliest version-matched recorded read whose canonical content/error differs on deterministic re-execution; after at least one downstream step; hidden injection labels excluded
dependency_rule: Model/user generations depend on observed prefix; calls depend on producing dispatch and prior writes; database-version-keyed read cache; conservative closure
safe_restore: Retail-only in-memory copy of agent/user states, pending message/routing, trajectory, local counters and DB; global attempt/time/usage counts never reset
primary_measure: Official evaluator reward conditional on fault exercised; also report unconditioned reward and coverage
failure_reporting: Provider/runtime/evaluator failures retained with null reward; fault not reached marked not exercised; no favorable-result replacement
analysis: Paired task/fault/seed results, denominators and coverage; descriptive intervals only with sample counts; no significance claim from pilot
notes: Faults are researcher-defined; public tasks/evaluator do not make the fault protocol an official recovery benchmark.
Seed does not guarantee identical provider output or deterministic paired trajectories.
Source rollback and selective recovery may coincide under conservative dependencies; do not tune faults to force an advantage.
Full matrix is planned, not yet completed. Published recovery methods are not relabeled as implemented.
v3 has offline correctness evidence only before new live trials; do not pool with earlier adapter versions. Cache-hit counts alone do not establish net work savings.
cache_reuse_rule: After selective recovery only; exact tool/arguments/requestor/DB-hash match; saved value independently revalidated against restored DB; detected source and errors excluded; writes never cached. Equal tool outputs do not establish reasoning independence.
timeout_semantics: Cooperative upstream timeout, not a hard deadline. Report elapsed time and overruns separately from official reward.
